title: How Citibank Lost $900,000,000 With One Click

sources.short: In re Citibank August 11, 2020 Wire Transfers, S.D.N.Y., Feb 16 2021
sources.fact: Citibank meant to wire about $7.8M in interest to Revlon lenders and wired about $893.9M of its own money; three people approved it (six-eyes); lenders kept about $504M; judge: one of the biggest blunders in banking history.
Headline: Citibank can't get back $500 million it wired by mistake, judge rules.

scenes.prompt: Cinematic night photo of Manhattan office towers from above, a few windows lit, cold blue tones, haze, 16:9, no text
scenes.head:
CITIBANK N.A.
OUTGOING WIRE TRANSFER

lines.say: At five forty five on a Tuesday evening one click sent nine hundred million dollars out of Citibank.
The money was gone before anyone at the bank looked up.

scenes.prompt: Cinematic 3D render of a huge round steel bank vault door standing open in a dark concrete room, one cold spotlight from above, dramatic shadows, 16:9, no text

lines.say: The bank asked for it back and a judge said no.

show.t: Citibank [can't get back $500 million] it wired by mistake, judge rules

lines.say: It meant to send eight million and it sent one hundred times more.

scenes.by: U.S. DISTRICT JUDGE JESSE FURMAN · FEBRUARY 16 2021

lines.say: The judge called it one of the biggest blunders in banking history.

show.t: one of the biggest blunders in banking history

lines.say: So who clicked and who kept the money and why did the law let them?

scenes.head: THE MOST EXPENSIVE CLICK IN BANKING

lines.say: This is the nine hundred million dollar click.
The payment leaves at five forty five and nobody notices until morning.
Then the bank asks for its money back and some lenders simply say no.
Almost nine hundred million went out and half a billion never came back.
